Renee M.: Heads up  planning time off question: if I transfer from FT to a part-time role mid-Dec, how does carryover work?
Kyle (People Ops): Hi Renee  your carryover is pro-rated based on your FTE on the carryover snapshot date (Dec 31). If youre part-time at that moment, the 40h cap is multiplied by your FTE (e.g., 0.5 FTE -> 20h cap).
Jorge P.: And accruals for the month of December  do we get a full month if were active on the last day?
Kyle (People Ops): We accrue monthly on the last payroll cycle. If youre active on the payroll snapshot date, you receive that months accrual prorated by days worked that pay period.
Renee M.: Suppose I have 38h PTO as FT and switch to 0.6 FTE. Will I be allowed to carry all 38h?
Kyle (People Ops): In that case the pro-rated cap would be 40h * 0.6 = 24h. Wed carry 24h automatically; the remaining 14h would expire unless an exception is approved.
Renee M.: How do exceptions work if its a role change not a leave?
Kyle (People Ops): Exceptions are discretionary. Please email people-ops@redwood.com with subject: "PTO Carryover Exception  Role Change  <Name>" including old/new FTE, remaining balance, and manager acknowledgement. Well review and generally approve if the change is HR-driven and not employee-initiated.
Jorge P.: What about holiday blackout rules? We have team holiday rotations around Dec 24-28. Any mandatory staffing?
Kyle (People Ops): We have two levels: soft blackout Dec 20Jan 2 (coordinate with manager) and mandatory coverage for a few core infra roles Dec 24-27. If youre on the mandatory rota your manager will notify you by Nov 15. Those dates require formal coverage plans and can't be declined unless exceptional circumstances.
Renee M.: If someone needs to use sick during the mandatory rota, how does that get handled?
Kyle (People Ops): Managers should use team swaps or bring on temporary coverage; for emergencies contact people-ops and your director. We try to be flexible for legitimate emergencies.
